issues.title: Missing Mozilla Public License header
issues.description: The rule requires that every .swift file begins with the exact Mozilla Public License header comment block at the top of the file. This file is missing the required header entirely.
issues.rule_name: All Swift Files Must Include Mozilla Public License Header

issues.title: Test completes without waiting for async image download
issues.description: The test was converted from async to synchronous but the expectation and wait statement were removed. This causes the test to complete immediately without waiting for the asynchronous image download callback to execute. The XCTAssert statements inside the completion handler will never be verified, resulting in false positive test passes even if the image download fails or produces incorrect results. This is a critical testing bug that undermines test reliability.

issues.title: Closure wrapper loses @Sendable annotation causing concurrency safety violation
issues.description: The moreButtonAction parameter is marked as @Sendable @MainActor to ensure thread-safe access in Swift 6 concurrency mode. However, the wrappedAction closure that wraps this action drops the @Sendable annotation, only keeping @MainActor. This breaks the sendability guarantee required by Swift 6, potentially allowing non-Sendable types to be captured and accessed from multiple threads unsafely. In Swift 6 strict concurrency mode, this will cause compiler errors or runtime crashes when the closure captures non-Sendable state.

issues.title: Async test assertion never verified due to missing expectation
issues.description: The test was updated to use @Sendable closures for Swift 6 concurrency compliance, but the expectation and wait statements were removed. The test now completes immediately without waiting for the asynchronous requestMediaCapturePermission callback. The XCTAssertEqual inside the decisionHandler closure will never execute, causing the test to always pass even when the media capture permission logic is broken. This is particularly problematic because this test validates critical permission handling behavior.

issues.title: Unsafe concurrency annotation on non-thread-safe static property
issues.description: The static generator property is marked with nonisolated(unsafe) despite the comment explicitly stating 'ContentBlockerGenerator is not thread safe'. This annotation bypasses Swift 6's concurrency safety checks and allows the non-thread-safe ContentBlockerGenerator to be accessed from multiple isolation domains without protection. This creates a potential data race condition where multiple threads could access the generator simultaneously, leading to undefined behavior, crashes, or data corruption. The unsafe annotation should only be used when the developer can guarantee thread safety through other means, which the comment explicitly contradicts.

issues.title: Static property missing explicit access control modifier
issues.description: Rule 11 requires explicit access control on properties/methods. The modified static property `generator` is declared without an explicit access modifier (e.g., `private`, `internal`, `public`).
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// FXIOS-14548 ContentBlockerGenerator is not thread safe
nonisolated(unsafe) static let generator = ContentBlockerGenerator.factory()
issues.rule_name: Rule 11: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31468 - Refactor FXIOS-14466 FXIOS-14463 [Swift 6 Migration] Migrate ShareTo and BrowserKit Package to Swift 6

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the BrowserKit package to Swift tools 6.2 and strips the experimental StrictConcurrency, RegionBasedIsolation, and InferSendableFromCaptures flags that Swift 6 now enables by default. It also bumps the ShareTo extension targets to SWIFT_VERSION 6.0 in the Xcode project, and adds @Sendable annotations and a small closure wrapper in the homepage section header. Most of the Package.swift churn is mechanical and correct, and I checked that all six ShareTo build configurations received the new setting.

The main problem is in the test changes. In `SVGImageProcessorTests`, the standard SVG test was converted to a synchronous method but lost both its expectation and its wait, so its assertions run in a Kingfisher callback that may fire after the test has already returned. That makes the test unable to fail reliably. A second test-infrastructure issue is that `@MainActor` was removed from `startMockImageServer` along with the comment explaining why it was needed. The license header was also dropped from `MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift`. Finally, the ShareTo "migration" contains no Swift source changes; the only change is the build setting, so whether ShareTo actually compiles cleanly under Swift 6 is unverified until CI reports back.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The standard SVG test no longer waits on its completion handler, so it can pass without checking anything. That is a test that can never fail, which is worse than no test. The removed main-actor guard and the dropped license header are smaller but real regressions. The Package.swift and project-file changes themselves look correct.

architecture.overview: BrowserKit is a local Swift package with many targets, each declaring its own Swift settings in BrowserKit/Package.swift. Before this PR, most targets opted into Swift 6 checking through experimental flags (StrictConcurrency, RegionBasedIsolation, InferSendableFromCaptures) on a tools-version 5.10 manifest. The PR raises the manifest to tools 6.2, where those behaviors are the default, so the per-target flags are removed. ShareTo is a separate app extension target in firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj; its six build configurations gain SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0. The only runtime-adjacent code change is in the homepage section header, which wraps an optional @Sendable @MainActor callback before handing it to ActionButtonViewModel.
steps: Start at BrowserKit/Package.swift: the manifest moves from tools 5.10 to 6.2, and each target's swiftSettings list loses the experimental feature flags.

Test targets such as SiteImageViewTests and WebEngineTests were updated alongside this so they compile under the stricter model; the async tests in SVGImageProcessorTests were converted to synchronous callbacks.
The ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator target adds nonisolated(unsafe) to its shared generator to satisfy the checker, with a ticket reference, instead of making the type thread-safe.
The ShareTo app extension is changed only in the Xcode project: each of its six build configurations is set to SWIFT_VERSION 6.0, with no source edits in the ShareTo folder.
LabelButtonHeaderView.configure accepts a @Sendable @MainActor action and wraps it in a closure before passing it to ActionButtonViewModel, which feeds ActionButton's touchUpInside handler.

findings.title: Standard SVG test no longer waits, so it can never fail
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift`, the test `testDownloadingSVGImage_withKingfisherProcessor_forStandardSVGCase` (around lines 12-37) calls `siteDownloader.downloadImage` and returns without waiting, so its XCTAssert calls inside the completion can run after the test has ended and cannot fail the test reliably. Restore an `XCTestExpectation`: create it before the download, call `exp.fulfill()` in both the success and failure branches, and finish the test with `wait(for: [exp], timeout: 2.0)`. Follow the pattern already used in `testDownloadingSVGImage_withKingfisherProcessor_forSpecialSVGCase` in the same file.

findings.title: Removed @MainActor guard from mock server and its explanatory comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift`, `startMockImageServer` (around line 208) previously had `@MainActor` and a comment explaining that GCDWebServer must first be initialized on the main thread. Both were removed in this PR, and the helper now runs from non-isolated test methods. Either restore `@MainActor` on the helper, with the comment, and make the calling tests isolated accordingly, or prove the initialization is safe on any thread and state that in a short comment. Match the isolation style used elsewhere in the BrowserKit test targets.

findings.title: MPL license header removed from MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift`, the MPL 2.0 license header (three comment lines at the top of the file) was removed by this PR, which is unrelated to the Swift 6 migration. Restore the exact header used in other BrowserKit source files, such as `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/WKUIHandlerTests.swift` lines 1-3, above the `import ContentBlockingGenerator` line.

findings.title: nonisolated(unsafe) silences the checker instead of fixing thread safety
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift`, the static `generator` property (around line 6) is marked `nonisolated(unsafe)` because `ContentBlockerGenerator` is not thread-safe (FXIOS-14548). The `main()` method (around line 10) calls it once. Consider creating the generator as a local inside `main()` so the unsafe annotation is not needed. Otherwise, keep the annotation and make sure the comment says the value is used only from a single call on the main entry point.

findings.title: Wrapper closure in LabelButtonHeaderView appears unnecessary
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Home/Homepage/SectionHeader/LabelButtonHeaderView.swift`, `configure(state:moreButtonAction:textColor:theme:)` (around lines 104-113) wraps `moreButtonAction` in a `wrappedAction` closure before creating `ActionButtonViewModel`. Check whether the optional `@Sendable @MainActor` action can be passed directly as `touchUpAction`, which would remove the wrapper. Confirm the code still compiles under Swift 6 and that the button does nothing when no action is provided, as it does now. Keep the change minimal.

findings.title: ShareTo migration contains no Swift source changes; Swift 6 readiness is unverified
findings.fixPrompt: The ShareTo app extension target (`F84B22481A0920C600AAB793`) now sets `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` in all six build configurations in `firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, but no ShareTo Swift sources were changed. Build the ShareTo scheme under Swift 6 mode and fix any concurrency diagnostics in the ShareTo sources, or state in the PR that the source audit is pending. Confirm the build is green in CI before merging.

findings.title: Swift tools 6.2 raises the minimum Xcode version for BrowserKit
findings.body:
`BrowserKit/Package.swift` now declares `swift-tools-version: 6.2`, so every consumer must build with a Swift 6.2 toolchain or newer. The Bitrise configuration in the repo runs against an iOS 26.1 simulator, which suggests Xcode 26 is already in use, so this is probably fine. Still, the requirement should be documented in the PR so that anyone using an older Xcode knows the bump is intentional.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Package.swift" lines="1-1"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Package.swift`, the manifest was bumped to `swift-tools-version: 6.2`. Confirm the CI and local Xcode versions used by this repo are at least Xcode 26 (Swift 6.2). Mention the new minimum toolchain in the PR description or a comment so contributors on older Xcode understand the requirement.

findings.title: Experimental feature flags removed in favor of Swift 6 defaults
findings.body:
Removing `StrictConcurrency`, `RegionBasedIsolation`, and `InferSendableFromCaptures` from each target is the right cleanup. With tools 6.2, Swift 6 language mode turns these behaviors on by default, so the flags were redundant and kept the manifest noisy. The result is a shorter, easier-to-read manifest with one shared baseline. The test targets that lost their flag lists keep empty `swiftSettings` arrays, which compile fine.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Package.swift" lines="87-100"}

findings.title: WKUIHandler test still exercises the callback after dropping its expectation
findings.body:
In `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess`, the expectation and `wait` were removed. This is safe because `WKUIHandler.requestMediaCapturePermission` calls the `decisionHandler` synchronously on every path, so the `XCTAssertEqual` in the closure always runs before the test returns. The handler is also typed `@Sendable`, which matches the new Swift 6 checking. Any regression that changes the decision would still fail this test.

::code{file="BrowserKit/Sources/WebEngine/WKWebview/WKUIHandler.swift" lines="175-184"}

findings.title: All ShareTo build configurations updated consistently
findings.body:
The ShareTo target's configuration list (`F84B22551A0920C600AAB793`) contains six configurations: Fennec, Fennec_Testing, Fennec_Enterprise, Firefox, FirefoxBeta, and FirefoxStaging. Each one got `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` in this PR, so no configuration is left on the old Swift version. Keeping the setting in step across every configuration is a good sign for the build. This is a positive finding, not a problem.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj" lines="29783-29786"}
